correction.text: Kuk Swamp "lies in the Wahgi Valley of the highlands at an altitude of about 1,550 metres" and is "some 12-13 kilometres northeast of Mount Hagen"; infobox "Location: Western Highlands Province, Papua New Guinea"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. A 40 km disc round Mount Hagen (19 land cells, about 4,800 km2) stands for the Wahgi Valley farmers; the page gives only the 116 ha heritage site (buffer 195 ha) and the 1,550 m highland setting, so the disc overstates the site by orders of magnitude and the real extent of New Guinea highland farming is unknown. Cliopatria has no shape.

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): the farmers of the Wahgi Valley have been draining and planting the Kuk swamp for a thousand years. "Archaeological evidence for early agricultural drainage systems was found here, beginning about 9,000 years ago"; taro and other plants were grown "at what would have been the edge of their cultivable limit in the highlands". Agriculture begins about 7050 BCE, before the floor.

4950 BCE: bananas and sugar cane join the crops at Kuk. "Additional archaeobotanical evidence, dated to between 6,900 and 6,400 years ago" (banana phytoliths between 6950 and 6550 years ago); 6,900 years BP is 4950 BCE.

ledger.note: 3400 BCE (end of the cultures horizon): the dossier stops here but Kuk farming continues. The dossier stops at -3400, the horizon of the cultures group (Cliopatria holds nothing before 3400 BCE and no later group draws this land until the colonies); the culture itself does not end there. The page gives no end to the Kuk drainage system.

certainty.note: A swamp-edge farming landscape with no recorded border.

sources.title: Kuk Swamp
sources.note: Early agriculture at Kuk, Wahgi Valley, Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea: drainage from about 9,000 years ago, bananas and sugar cane 6,900-6,400 years ago; heritage area 116 ha.

notes: Kuk Swamp, Wahgi Valley, Papua New Guinea. The page does not describe the drainage phases (the question asked for Phases 1 to 6 returned page silent). The dossier is a site-based placement, the only dated early-farming culture the brief names for New Guinea; lowland and coastal New Guinea (Papuan foragers, the Bismarck obsidian trade) are blank. Ends at -3400 by the group's convention.
